title: Practice with friends
hook: a walking friend, a reading friend: in the desert, Arsenius fled people and Antony said our life is with our neighbor
tomorrow: Ananda said good friends are half the path. what did the Buddha say?

segments.voice: Small ones: in Mark, the children get arms and a blessing before any lesson. Today, the friends. And two old monks who'd have argued about it.

A running club at dawn, or a solo run with earbuds in and no one to wait for: runners split on it, and each side swears by theirs. The desert monks of Egypt had the same split, about God. A man named Arsenius had lived at the palace. Tradition says he prayed: Lord, lead me to be saved. And a voice answered: Arsenius, flee from people. So he did. He ran from everyone, even the brothers who loved him.
screen: `A CLUB AT DAWN, OR EARBUDS ALONE.` → `ARSENIUS LEAVES THE PALACE.` → `FLEE FROM PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: View one. The sayings of the desert elders remember a second word Arsenius heard: flee, be silent, pray. Once a monk named Mark asked him straight out: why do you avoid us? Arsenius said: God knows I love you. But I cannot be with God and with people at the same time. That's the best case for solitude. Not coldness. A man who knew that, for him, company drowned out the voice he'd come to hear. View two. Antony, the old father of the desert monks, put it the other way: our life and our death is with our neighbor. If we gain our brother, we have gained God. For Antony, the neighbor isn't a distraction from God. The neighbor is where you meet God, or fail to. And the tradition didn't pick a winner. Both sayings sit in the same collection. Christian monks went on living both ways: hermits alone in cells, and brothers in communities. Even the hermits walked to an elder to ask for a word, and a brother would come knocking. So the desert's answer to practice with friends isn't always, and it isn't never. It's knowing which kind of monk you are this season, and keeping at least one friend in it.
screen: `VIEW ONE: FLEE, BE SILENT, PRAY.` · `I CANNOT BE WITH GOD AND WITH PEOPLE.` · `VIEW TWO: OUR LIFE IS WITH OUR NEIGHBOR.` · `BOTH KEPT IN ONE BOOK.` · then, large: `A FRIEND IN IT.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who might share one piece of your practice: a walk, a reading, a quiet coffee. Write the invitation as a one-line text, and if it feels right, send it after the sit. For the rest of the sit, hold their face in mind and breathe.
Practice with friends: a walking friend, a reading friend, someone in it with you, the way even the desert hermits had a brother at the door.
Your line: a friend in it. Arsenius fled, Antony stayed, and the desert kept both. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Christian monastic life has long held both hermits and communities. People on many paths keep a walking friend, a reading partner or a small group that meets to practice together.

fork.setup: a friend says she keeps her practice private because people distract her. what's the best case for her side, as the desert kept it?
options: like Arsenius, some need distance to hear God at all, and can love people from there.
she's just shy; every desert monk said practice belongs in a group.

fork.reveal: Arsenius said he loved the brothers but couldn't be with God and with people at once. The tradition kept his saying right beside Antony's.

trapdoor: what you thought: spiritual practice is either a solo thing or a group thing.
what it means: the desert kept both: Arsenius fled people, Antony found God in the neighbor.
what a scholar hears: the Sayings of the Desert Fathers file both men's words side by side in one collection, with no verdict between them.
guess: sharing one piece of your practice with a friend, like a walk
a group retreat run by a teacher, with everyone silent
doing your practice alone, then telling friends about it

chat.says: theo wants me in his saturday walking group. my walks are my alone time though. do i say no?
options: The desert kept both: Arsenius fled, Antony stayed near the neighbor. Keep your walk; join one Saturday.
Say no. The desert monks all agreed that real practice only happens alone, with nobody else around.
Say yes and drop your solo walks for good; Antony showed that being alone was a mistake.
chat.meaning: The desert kept Arsenius's solitude and Antony's neighbor side by side. Neither cancels the other; the question is which this season needs.

tie.story: Arsenius fled people to hear God, and Antony said our life is with our neighbor; the desert kept both.
tie.friend: Zoe can keep her solo walks and still let Theo be a friend in it on Saturdays.

Arsenius.meaning: a desert monk who had lived at the palace and fled people

Antony.meaning: an early desert monk of Egypt, called a father of monks

desert monks.meaning: Christian monks and hermits who lived in the Egyptian desert

elder.meaning: an experienced monk others asked for a word of advice
